trial_court: Additional Judge to the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Gwalior in RCSHM No. 429-A/2021
case_name: Brahmswaroop Sharma (Dead) Through Lr ... vs Smt Kiran Sharma

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Brahmswaroop Sharma (Dead) Through Lr Ashwini Kumar, son

facts_of_case: 75-year-old retired Company Commander lost his wife and published an advertisement seeking a bride for his son. Respondent contacted him, began visiting his house, and allegedly concealed her previous marriages and obtained a fabricated marriage certificate. Plaintiff asserts that respondent was already married to Ashok Sharma and had earlier married Aashiq Kalbhor.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage certificate by itself is not proof of a valid marriage; factum of marriage must be independently proved.
legal_principles.held: It is argued that a marriage certificate by itself is not proof of a valid marriage; factum of marriage must be independently proved.
cited_cases: Dolly Rani v. Manish Kumar Chanchal, (2025) 2 SCC 487

legal_principles.principle: Where a Hindu marriage is not performed in accordance with prescribed rites and ceremonies, including Saptpadi, such a marriage cannot be construed as a valid Hindu marriage under law.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that where a Hindu marriage is not performed in accordance with prescribed rites and ceremonies, including Saptpadi, such a marriage cannot be construed as a valid Hindu marriage under law.

outcome.final_order: Instant First Appeal under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act, 1984 has been preferred by Ashwini Kumar, legal representative (son) of original plaintiff late Brahmswaroop Sharma assailing the judgment and decree dated 02.09.2024 passed by Additional Judge to the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Gwalior.

use_for_drafting: drafting a property dispute appeal in Family Court Gwalior
advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications for a Company Commander's family
assisting with a permanent injunction application in a family law case
